What Happens When AI Lets You Do Pieces of Everyone Else’s Job? Crossover Read this article on LinkedIn to join the conversation Read on LinkedIn In this edition AI is turning job boundaries into trading lanes, with tasks moving freely between professions. OpenAI’s latest research shows task crossover is already blurring old professional borders, with people doing work that used to belong to entirely different roles. So we’re digging into cross-stack careers, the great role rebundling, smaller outcome-driven teams, and why your next big career move will come from owning work WAY beyond the borders of your current job title. 🛠️ The Role Rebundling Edition 🛠️ By Andrew Allen and Carla Dewing ⚡ Your Job Description Has Stopped Making Sense... What happens AFTER AI takes pieces of your job? Apparently, it starts handing you pieces of everyone else’s. In a recent article, we looked at task unbundling - AI stripping routine work out of jobs and exposing the tender expertise underneath. OpenAI’s new Work at the Frontier research reveals the next BIG move. 43.5% of occupation-specific AI use already involves work historically associated with another profession. Designers are pulling in analysis and marketing. Marketers are troubleshooting technical problems and running financial work. Engineers are exporting technical capabilities into everybody else’s stack. OpenAI calls it task crossover. We think what follows is even bigger: TASK UNBUNDLING → TASK CROSSOVER → ROLE REBUNDLING When people can carry work further across old professional boundaries, companies eventually have to rebuild the jobs around them. And some professions are already crossing those boundaries hard . ...
